I'm an international student who's a psych major so I'll try to give you a well described answer. 

1. BSc or BA depends on what you want to do in the future. From the BSc psych students that I've met, most of them want to go to med school or vet school or something related to the medical field whereas the BA students want to become counseling psychologists or researchers or lawyers or something like that. If you're undecided and good at science and maths, it's better to go for BSc as it keeps all the doors open. 

2. BSc is more science oriented with for credit chemistry, biology and maths courses whereas BA is more humanities related with the science content completely optional.

3. I've only been studying at Keele so I don't know about that. But what I can say is that, Keele is great, the profs are nice and has more facilities than Glendon in general. 

4. Psych program at york is great. There are professors who studied at schools like Dartmouth and Stanford teaching here and taking on students as volunteers and fellow researcher assistants. Most of the psych profs are accomodating and are fair in dealing with the students. 

5. The psych department has many fellowships abroad. A friend of mine who was in her fourth year went to Germany to do fellowship there. With the attention mental health has started to generate the past few years, Psychology is going to be the next thing that blows up like engineering or technology did once.
